title: Boss: The Wrong Total
story: A report asks for categories with more than one product, but it crashes and groups by the wrong column.
goal: Fix the query: show each category and its product count n, only for categories with more than 1 product.
starter:
SELECT category, COUNT(*)
FROM products
WHERE COUNT(*) > 1
GROUP BY name;

tests.label: Hidden check on other data
Hidden check on other data

hints: Aggregates such as COUNT() are not allowed in WHERE. What clause filters groups?
Group by category, not by name.
SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n FROM products GROUP BY category HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
socratic: What error does the query give?
Compare the rows you got with the rows expected. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what was wrong with the query, and how did you fix it?
solution: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n FROM products GROUP BY category HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
alt: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS n FROM products GROUP BY category HAVING n > 1;
